Acacia dealbata: In many habitats by streams, gullies and alpine ridges. Dry forests.
Achillea millefolium: Meadows, pastures, lawns etc. on all but the poorest soils.
Aconitum napellus: Damp shady places and moist rich meadows in southern Wales and south-western England. It is usually found in calcareous soils.
Acorus calamus: Found in moist soils and shallow water in ditches, marshes, river edges and ponds.
Alchemilla vulgaris: Moist meadows, open woods, pastures and also on rock ledges in mountainous areas.
Allium sativum: Not known in a truly wild situation.
Aloe ferox: Abundant on arid rocky hillsides up to 1,000 metres altitude. Also found in grassy fynbos and on the edges of the karoo. It grows both in the open and in bushy areas.
Althaea officinalis: The upper margins of salt and brackish marshes, sides of ditches and grassy banks near the sea.
Andrographis paniculata: Village groves, roadsides, waste places, open sandy locations and fields, but also in monsoon and teak forest receiving only 10-20% of full light, at elevations from sea level to 1,600 metres.
Anethum graveolens: Fields, waste places etc in the Mediterranean.
Arctium lappa: Waste ground, preferring calcareous soils, it is sometimes also found in meadows and woods.
Arctostaphylos uva-ursi: Dry open woods, often on gravelly or sandy soils. It is also found on sand dunes along the coast and is also found on limestone in the European Alps.
Armoracia rusticana: Arable land, waste ground and by streams, favouring slightly damp positions.
Arnica montana: Calcareous soils in mountain pastures. Found especially on granite or siliceous soils in the Alps, up to 2500 metres. Pasture and open woodland, usually on poorer acid soils.
Artemisia annua: Occurs naturally as part of a steppe vegetation in the northern parts of Chahar and Suiyuan provinces in China, at 1000 to 1500 m above sea level.
Artemisia dracunculus: By rivers and streams. Grassland and arid steppe.
Artemisia vulgaris: Common on hedgebanks and waysides, uncultivated and waste land.
Asparagus racemosus: Found at elevations up to 1,200 metres in the Himalayas, eastwards from Kashmir. Broad-leaved forests along streams or valleys at elevations of 2100 - 2200 metres in western China.
Astragalus membranaceus: Dry sandy soils. Mountain thickets. Steppes, meadows, xerophytic shrubs, coniferous forests; montane belt at altitudes of 800 - 2000 metres.
Atropa belladonna: Woods, thickets and hedges, mainly on calcareous soils.
Bacopa monnieri: Mud flats in estuarine habitats. Moist and wet places, such as the borders of water channels, wells, irrigated fields etc.
Berberis vulgaris: Light deciduous woodland, hedges, roadsides, clearings etc, preferring a sunny position and a chalky soil.
Betula pendula: Open woodland and heaths. Rarely found on chalk.
Borago officinalis: Waste ground near houses in Britain.
Calendula officinalis: The original habitat is obscure but it is found as a garden escape on waste, cultivated and arable land and along roadsides.
Camellia sinensis: Shaded areas at an elevation of 2100 - 2700 metres in Yunnan.
Cananga odorata: Moist evergreen forests and teak forests. From sea level to mid-montane elevations. Common in secondary forest formations and along forest edges in Vietnam.
Cannabis sativa: Fluvial deposits on crags and stony slopes. It is occasionally found as a casual on waste ground in Britain. It is especially found as a weed of nitrogen-rich soils near human habitations
Capsella bursa-pastoris: Arable land, gardens, waste places etc, it is a common weed of cultivated soil.
Carum carvi: Moist meadows, arable land and waste places from lowland to mountain elevations.
Centella asiatica: Old stone walls and rocky sunny places in lowland hills and especially by the coast in central and southern Japan. Shady, damp and wet places such as paddy fields, and in grass thickets.
Chamaemelum nobile: Sandy commons, pastures and grassy roadsides.
Chelidonium majus: Rubble, damp ground, banks, hedgerows and by walls, nearly always close to human habitations.
Chrysanthemum morifolium: Not known in a truly wild situation.
Cichorium intybus: Grassy meadows and arable land, especially on chalk.
Citrus aurantium: Original habitat is obscure, possibly a back cross involving C. maxima X C. reticulata.
Citrus bergamia: Original habitat is obscure, possibly a back cross involving C. maxima X C. reticulata.
Citrus limon: Original habitat is obscure, probably a hybrid involving C. medica x C. aurantifolia.
Clinopodium vulgare: Heaths and dry grassy places, usually on calcareous soils.
Cnicus benedictus: Dry sunny places in arable, stony and waste ground.
Commiphora mukul: Rocky and open hilly areas or rough terrain and sandy tracts in warm and semiarid to arid areas at elevations from 250 - 1,800 metres.
Commiphora myrrha: Thickets in desert scrubland. Open Acacia, Commiphora bushland on shallow soil, chiefly over limestone at elevations from 250 - 1,300 metres.
Convallaria majalis: Dry shady woodland, usually on calcareous soils, and especially in ash woodlands.
Coptis chinensis: Damp coniferous woods and bogs. Forests, shaded places in valleys at elevations of 500 - 2000 metres.
Coriandrum sativum: Waste places and arable land, often by the sides of rivers.
Crataegus monogyna: Woods, hedges, thickets etc, on most soils except wet peat and poor acid sands.
Crocus sativus: Not known in a truly wild location.
Cuminum cyminum: Not known in a truly wild condition.
Cupressus sempervirens: Rocky mountainous areas, usually near the coast, in S. Europe.
Datura stramonium: Dry waste ground and amongst rubble or the ruins of old buildings.
Digitalis purpurea: Acid soils in woods, heaths, mountain grasslands etc.
Echinacea purpurea: Dry open woods, prairies and barrens.
Eleutherococcus senticosus: Mixed and coniferous mountain forests, forming small undergrowth or groups in thickets and edges. Sometimes found in oak groves at the foot of cliffs, very rarely in high forest riparian woodland.
Elymus repens: A common weed of gardens, fields, hedgerows and meadows.
Eucalyptus globulus: Damp marshy areas on moist loams and clays. Found in hilly country or moist valleys in deep rich soils.
Euphrasia officinalis: Moist grassland and chalky pastures, semi-parasitic on grass.
Ficus carica: Amongst rocks, in woods and scrub on hot dry soils.
Ficus elastica: Hill forest, particularly on cliffs and limestone hills.
Foeniculum vulgare: Found most often in dry stony calcareous soils near the sea.
Fragaria vesca: Shaded, fairly damp places in woodland.
Frangula alnus: Swamps and damp places, usually on moist heaths and damp open woods, preferring a peaty soil.
Frangula purshiana: Rich bottom lands and sides of canyons, usually in coniferous forests.
